item.title: Somalia looks to the future as the UN's political mission closes
item.description: “The story of the UN's political engagement in Somalia has been one of persistence, partnership and adaptation,” Raisedon Zenenga, the UN Secretary-General's Deputy Special Representative for Somalia has said, as three decades of UN political missions in the Horn of Africa country comes to an end on 31 October.

item.title: DPR Korea: Isolation deepens even as the country changes, says UN rights official
item.description: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is building factories and hospitals, rolling out smartphones and mobile banking, and passing new laws at an unprecedented rate. But its people are more cut off from the outside world than at any point in the country’s history.

item.title: Samarkand: A ‘living museum’ on the Silk Road grapples with a tourism boom
item.description: As the sun sets over Samarkand’s majestic Registan, its last rays glint across the turquoise mosaics. Dusk settles on the ancient square where great trade routes have crossed for centuries.

item.title: ‘They deserve to know the truth’: UN rights chief demands probe into staffer’s death in Houthi custody
item.description: The UN human rights chief on Saturday demanded an independent investigation into the death of a Yemeni colleague held by the Houthis for more than two years, whose family learned of his death only weeks after it happened.
